questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers is 35 and their product is 286. The positive difference between them is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the standard algebraic relation: (Difference)² = (Sum)² − 4 × (Product)

⇒ (Difference)² = 35² − 4 × 286

⇒ (Difference)² = 1225 − 1144 = 81

⇒ Difference = √81 = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Sum of two numbers** (x + y) = 35 and their **Product** (xy) = 286.

Formula Used: (x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1eb3fd2ea154f3e499218d7de11006395c067d147a8b41fa088e85c5a041de48.png] 

⇒ Let the two **positive numbers** be x and y.

⇒ x + y = 35

⇒ xy = 286

⇒ (x − y)² = (35)² − 4(286)

⇒ (x − y)² = 1225 − 1144

⇒ (x − y)² = 81

⇒ x − y = √81 = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quadratic Form Relation

If sum (S) and product (P) are known, the numbers are roots of the equation: t² − St + P = 0.

Basic Algebraic Identities

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab. Subtracting these gives (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Factorization Method

For xy = 286, find factors such that they add to 35. Factors of 286 are 1, 2, 11, 13, 22, 26, 143, 286. Here 22 + 13 = 35.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price. He then allows two successive discounts of 18% and 5% on the marked price. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **effective percentage change** formula: Net % = x + y + (x × y)/100.

Combine **Mark-up** (+40%) and first **Discount** (−18%): 40 − 18 − (40 × 18)/100 = 14.8%.

Combine result (+14.8%) and second **Discount** (−5%): 14.8 − 5 − (14.8 × 5)/100 = 9.8 − 0.74 = 9.06%.

Since the net result is positive, it represents a **Profit Percentage**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.06%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mark-up Percentage** = 40%

**Successive Discounts** = 18% and 5%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Mark-up/100)

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

Profit % = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/627e19c071e413f878b858b614fb2a7d2944c16700d9468467d264d6dc41f385.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 40% of 100 = 140

⇒ Price after 18% discount = 140 × (100 − 18)/100 = 140 × 0.82

⇒ Price after 18% discount = 114.8

⇒ Price after 5% discount (SP) = 114.8 × (100 − 5)/100 = 114.8 × 0.95

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 109.06

⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 109.06 − 100 = 9.06

⇒ **Profit %** = (9.06 / 100) × 100 = 9.06%

**∴ The correct answer is 9.06%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

Total discount for two rates d₁ and d₂ is given by: dₙₑₜ = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100.

Profit and Discount Relation

The relationship between CP and MP is: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

Markup and Profit

**Mark-up** is the value added to CP to reach MP. **Profit** is the final gain after all discounts on MP.

questions.question: A sum of ₹8,000 is invested at a compound interest rate of 12.5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually. What is the compound interest earned?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate **12.5%** = 1/8 in fraction.

Ratio of **Principal** (P) to **Amount** (A) for 1 year = 8 : 9.

For 2 years, Ratio P : A = 8² : 9² = 64 : 81.

**Compound Interest** (CI) = 81 − 64 = 17 units.

64 units = ₹8,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 8,000 ÷ 64 = 125.

CI = 17 × 125 = ₹2,125.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal** (P) = ₹8,000

**Rate** (R) = 12.5% per annum

**Time** (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

Compound Interest (CI) = Amount − Principal

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd60dcb1485533d6fd8f8768ffc82f332ba05a3ba85efa0e40d61d812270c980.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 8,000 × (1 + 12.5/100)²

⇒ A = 8,000 × (1 + 1/8)²

⇒ A = 8,000 × (9/8) × (9/8)

⇒ A = 125 × 81

⇒ A = ₹10,125

⇒ CI = 10,125 − 8,000

⇒ CI = ₹2,125

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate

For two years at rate R%, the effective compound interest rate is R + R + (R × R)/100.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, CI − SI = P × (R/100)².

Compounding Periods

If compounded half-yearly, the rate becomes R/2 and the time period becomes 2n.

questions.question: The price of an article is increased by 25%. By what percentage should the increased price be reduced so that it becomes equal to the original price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct formula for **percentage reduction** to restore the original value: [r / (100 + r)] × 100.

Here, r = 25.

Reduction = [25 / (100 + 25)] × 100

Reduction = (25 / 125) × 100 = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Increase** in price = 25%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Percentage Reduction** = (Difference / Increased Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da315483443d85e3520ed562899a605914899eb314589b701d6ab2b21642e43f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **original price** of the article be ₹100.

⇒ Increased price = 100 + 25% of 100 = 100 + 25 = ₹125.

⇒ To return to the **original price** (₹100), the reduction required = 125 − 100 = ₹25.

⇒ Required **percentage reduction** = (25 / 125) × 100

⇒ Required percentage reduction = (1 / 5) × 100

⇒ Required percentage reduction = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base Change Rule

If quantity A is r% more than B, then B is [r / (100 + r)] × 100% less than A. If A is r% less than B, then B is [r / (100 − r)] × 100% more than A.

Fractional Equivalents

25% is equivalent to 1/4. When a value increases by 1/n, it must be decreased by 1/(n+1) to return to its original value. Here, n=4, so reduction = 1/(4+1) = 1/5 = 20%.

Net Percentage Change

For two successive percentage changes a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (ab / 100)]%. To result in zero net change, the formula must equate to 0.

⇒ 5.25 + 2.75 − 0.6 − (2/5 × 1/2)

⇒ 8.00 − 0.6 − (1/5)

⇒ 8 − 0.6 − 0.2

⇒ 8 − 0.8

⇒ 7.2

BODMAS Rule

questions.question: Simplify: 15 + (12)/(cot² A) - (12)/(cos² A)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given **trigonometric expression** into **tangent** and **secant** forms: 15 + 12 tan² A − 12 sec² A.

Factor out the common term 12: 15 + 12(tan² A − sec² A).

Apply the **Pythagorean identity**: Since sec² A − tan² A = 1, then tan² A − sec² A = −1.

The expression simplifies to: 15 + 12(−1) = 15 − 12 = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 15 + 12/cot² A − 12/cos² A

**Formula Used:** 1/cot A = tan A and 1/cos A = sec A; sec² A − tan² A = 1

⇒ Expression = 15 + 12 × (1/cot² A) − 12 × (1/cos² A)

⇒ Expression = 15 + 12 tan² A − 12 sec² A

⇒ Expression = 15 + 12(tan² A − sec² A)

⇒ From the identity sec² A − tan² A = 1, we know tan² A − sec² A = −1

⇒ Expression = 15 + 12(−1)

⇒ Expression = 15 − 12 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

There are three fundamental identities: sin² A + cos² A = 1, 1 + tan² A = sec² A, and 1 + cot² A = cosec² A.

Reciprocal Relations

Trigonometric ratios are related as follows: tan A = 1/cot A, sec A = 1/cos A, and cosec A = 1/sin A.

Simplification Rule

When simplifying trigonometric expressions, always look to convert terms into sine/cosine or use established identities to reduce variables.

questions.question: The largest four-digit number which when divided by 6, 14 and 7 leaves remainder 5 in each case is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of divisors 6, 14, and 7, which is **42**.

The largest 4-digit multiple of **42** is **9996** (calculated as 9999 − 3).

Adding the remainder: 9996 + 5 = 10001 (This is a **5-digit number**).

Subtract the LCM to find the previous valid number: 10001 − 42 = **9959**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9959.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: **6, 14, 7**

Remainder: **5**

Target: **Largest 4-digit number**

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = [**LCM**(Divisors) × k] + **Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5d00466eb8a8a1976a6c0763a50ff90a2679b9fc961acb5022085ccecf61630.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **LCM**(6, 14, 7) = **42**

⇒ **Largest 4-digit number** = 9999

⇒ 9999 ÷ 42 = 238 (Quotient), 3 (Remainder)

⇒ **Largest 4-digit multiple** of 42 = 9999 − 3 = **9996**

⇒ Check 4-digit constraint: 9996 + 5 = **10001** (Not a 4-digit number)

⇒ Previous multiple of 42 = 9996 − 42 = **9954**

⇒ **Required number** = 9954 + 5 = **9959**

**∴ The correct answer is 9959.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder Concept

When a number N is divided by a, b, c and leaves the same remainder 'r' in each case, then N = **LCM(a, b, c) × k + r**, where k is an integer.

Divisibility by 14

A number is divisible by **14** if it is simultaneously divisible by its co-prime factors **2 and 7**.

Successive Division vs Single Remainder

If remainders are different (r₁, r₂, r₃), and the difference (divisor − remainder) is constant 'd', then the number N = **LCM(divisors) × k − d**.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 56 cm. Its length is 4 cm more than twice its breadth. Find the breadth.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **Length** and **Breadth** = Half of **Perimeter** = 56 ÷ 2 = 28 cm.

Let **Breadth** be x, then **Length** = 2x + 4.

⇒ (2x + 4) + x = 28

⇒ 3x = 24 ⇒ x = 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Perimeter** of **Rectangle** = 56 cm

⇒ **Length** (L) = 4 + 2 × **Breadth** (B)

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Perimeter** = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38accaa57d462bef500aea804c2360e4f572d04b5dd7bd33b8604778b74fa8c1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (L + B) = 56

⇒ L + B = 56 ÷ 2

⇒ L + B = 28

Substitute L = 2B + 4 in the equation:

⇒ (2B + 4) + B = 28

⇒ 3B + 4 = 28

⇒ 3B = 28 − 4

⇒ 3B = 24

⇒ B = 24 ÷ 3

⇒ B = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is given by the product of its dimensions: Area = Length × Breadth.

Diagonal of Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners can be found using the Pythagorean theorem: Diagonal = √(Length² + Breadth²).

Perimeter of a Square

A square is a special rectangle where Length = Breadth = s. Its perimeter is 4 × s.

questions.question: In a division sum, the divisor is 5 times the quotient and 4 times the remainder. If the remainder is 15, what is the dividend?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **Remainder** = 15.

**Divisor** = 4 × 15 = 60.

**Quotient** = 60 ÷ 5 = 12.

**Dividend** = (60 × 12) + 15 = 720 + 15 = 735.

**∴ The correct answer is 735.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In a **division sum**:

**Remainder** (R) = 15

**Divisor** (D) = 4 × R

**Divisor** (D) = 5 × **Quotient** (Q)

**Formula Used:**

**Dividend** = (**Divisor** × **Quotient**) + **Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d756f36da9210c3de15f7fbef2872b77dd1aaece8fd91d3988f5820c0b2c4e5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Divisor** = 4 × 15 = 60

⇒ 60 = 5 × **Quotient**

⇒ **Quotient** = 60 ÷ 5 = 12

⇒ **Dividend** = (60 × 12) + 15

⇒ **Dividend** = 720 + 15

⇒ **Dividend** = 735

**∴ The correct answer is 735.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division Algorithm

For any two integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.

Properties of Remainder

The remainder is always a non-negative integer and is strictly less than the divisor. If the remainder is 0, the dividend is perfectly divisible by the divisor.

Verification Rule

To verify a division result, subtract the remainder from the dividend; the result must be the product of the divisor and the quotient.

questions.question: What is the digit y if the number 6y512 is exactly divisible by both 8 and 9?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **divisibility by 9**, the **sum of digits** must be a multiple of 9.

Sum of digits in 6y512 = 6 + y + 5 + 1 + 2 = 14 + y.

The nearest multiple of 9 after 14 is 18.

∴ 14 + y = 18 ⇒ y = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The number 6y512 is divisible by both **8** and **9**.

**Step 1: Check Divisibility by 8**

A number is divisible by 8 if its **last three digits** are divisible by 8.

⇒ Last three digits = 512.

⇒ 512 ÷ 8 = 64 (Remainder = 0).

Since 512 is divisible by 8, the number 6y512 is divisible by 8 for any single digit value of y.

**Step 2: Check Divisibility by 9**

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 9.

⇒ Sum = 6 + y + 5 + 1 + 2

⇒ Sum = 14 + y

For the number to be divisible by 9, (14 + y) must be 18, 27, etc.

Since y is a single digit (0 to 9):

⇒ 14 + y = 18

⇒ y = 18 − 14

⇒ y = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8 or if the last three digits are zero.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is exactly divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 72

Since 72 = 8 × 9 (co-prime factors), a number is divisible by 72 only if it is divisible by both 8 and 9 simultaneously.

questions.question: A solid cube is melted and half of its material is recast into a cuboid whose length, breadth, and height are in the ratio 2 : 1 : 1. The difference between the volume of the original cube and the cuboid formed is 250 cm³. Find the total surface area of the cuboid.

⇒ TSA = 2 × (10 × 5 + 5 × 5 + 5 × 10).

⇒ TSA = 2 × (50 + 25 + 50) = 2 × 125.

⇒ **TSA = 250 cm²**.

questions.question: Find the third proportional to 6 and 12.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **third proportional** (c) for two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated using the formula: **c = b² ÷ a**.

Given: **a = 6** and **b = 12**.

Substituting the values: **c = 12² ÷ 6**

**c = 144 ÷ 6 = 24**.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First number (**a**) = 6, Second number (**b**) = 12.

**Formula Used:** If three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c** are in **continued proportion**, then **a : b :: b : c** or **a/b = b/c**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19b980a396cd2c13c4d9326ffc36a7e12867e82fe0f62930627a2aad71c52484.png] 

⇒ Let the **third proportional** be **c**.

⇒ According to the definition: 6 : 12 :: 12 : **c**

⇒ 6 ÷ 12 = 12 ÷ **c**

⇒ 1 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ **c**

⇒ **c** = 12 × 2

⇒ **c** = 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is given by the square root of their product: **Mean = √(a × b)**.

Fourth Proportional

For four numbers **a**, **b**, **c**, and **d** to be in proportion (a : b :: c : d), the **fourth proportional** **d** is calculated as **(b × c) ÷ a**.

Continued Proportion

A series of numbers are in **continued proportion** if the ratio of any term to the next term is constant (a/b = b/c = c/d ...).

questions.question: Two bags contain marbles in the ratio 5 : 7. If 12 marbles are transferred from the second bag to the first bag, the ratio of marbles in the two bags becomes 7 : 5. Find the original number of marbles in the second bag.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial sum of ratios: 5 + 7 = 12 units; Final sum: 7 + 5 = 12 units.

Since the **total marbles** remain constant, compare the ratio parts directly.

Change in Bag 2: 7 units → 5 units = **2 units decrease**.

Given transfer = **12 marbles** ⇒ 2 units = 12 marbles.

1 unit = 6 marbles; **Original Bag 2** = 7 units × 6 = 42 marbles.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 marbles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial ratio of marbles in **Bag 1** and **Bag 2** = 5 : 7

Number of **marbles transferred** from Bag 2 to Bag 1 = 12

Final ratio of marbles = 7 : 5

**Formula Used:**

If original values are ax and bx, and k is transferred: (ax + k) / (bx − k) = m / n

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02e578233581be55ba9702c727208043fa3a972c36245c30d9ce219461fdc6c0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **original number** of marbles be 5x and 7x.

⇒ According to the question: (5x + 12) / (7x − 12) = 7 / 5

⇒ 5 × (5x + 12) = 7 × (7x − 12)

⇒ 25x + 60 = 49x − 84

⇒ 49x − 25x = 60 + 84

⇒ 24x = 144

⇒ x = 144 ÷ 24 = 6

⇒ **Original marbles in Bag 2** = 7x = 7 × 6 = 42

**∴ The correct answer is 42 marbles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Constant Sum

When items are transferred between two bags, the **total quantity** remains unchanged. Scaling ratios to have the same sum allows for **direct comparison** of units.

Inverse Proportion

If the product of two variables is constant, they are in **inverse proportion**. In this case, the total count is fixed, so an increase in one bag must result in a decrease in the other.

Proportionality Constant (x)

The constant x converts a ratio into **actual values**. Multiplying each term of the ratio by x gives the real quantity of the objects involved.

questions.question: If a square’s diagonal is extended by 6 units beyond a vertex, forming a triangle outside the square, what is the angle between this extension and the adjacent side of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **diagonal** of a **square** always acts as the **angle bisector** of the 90° vertex angle.

Therefore, the angle between the **diagonal** and any **adjacent side** is exactly 45°.

Since an **extension** of a straight line does not change its orientation, the **acute angle** formed between the extension of the diagonal and the **adjacent side** remains 45°.

In standard geometry, the angle between two intersecting lines is typically measured as the **acute angle** unless specified otherwise.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 degrees.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A **square** ABCD where the **diagonal** AC is extended by 6 units to point E.

**Formula Used:**

1. Interior angle of a square = 90°

2. Angle between the diagonal and side of a square = 45°

3. Angles on a straight line (linear pair) sum to 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d75cb3c4a29d1952008b7b79bf3f33bdd922c808111a7cb01ea8ad2f53f0eab.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In **square** ABCD, the interior angle ∠BCD = 90°.

⇒ The **diagonal** AC bisects ∠BCD, so ∠ACB = 45° and ∠ACD = 45°.

⇒ Line ACE is a straight line because it is an **extension** of the diagonal.

⇒ The **adjacent side** to the extension at vertex C is either BC or CD.

⇒ The angle between the extension CE and side BC is ∠BCE.

⇒ Since ∠ACB + ∠BCE = 180° (Linear Pair), then ∠BCE = 180° − 45° = 135°.

⇒ In geometry, the **angle between two lines** is often considered the **acute angle**.

⇒ Acute angle = 180° − 135° = 45°.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 degrees.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Square

The diagonal of a square with side s is given by d = s√2 and always bisects the vertex angles into 45° each.

Linear Pair of Angles

Angles on a straight line that share a common vertex and side sum up to 180°, forming a supplementary pair.

Angle between Lines

When two lines intersect, they form two pairs of angles; the smaller angle (0° to 90°) is typically defined as the angle between the lines.

questions.question: The average of five numbers 7, 11, 15, x, and 23 is 15. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **Average** problem, the sum of **deviations** from the mean must be zero.

Deviations from 15: (7−15) = −8, (11−15) = −4, (15−15) = 0, (23−15) = +8.

Net deviation of known numbers = −8 + (−4) + 0 + 8 = −4.

To balance the **Average**, the deviation of **x** must be +4.

**x** = 15 + 4 = 19.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers = 7, 11, 15, x, 23 | Total count (n) = 5 | **Average** = 15

**Formula Used:** **Average** = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c3a02745df3e3210760abc45bde31463fdfdaf493b82ae7448562b47362cc5e.png] 

⇒ Total **Sum** = **Average** × Number of terms

⇒ 7 + 11 + 15 + x + 23 = 15 × 5

⇒ 56 + x = 75

⇒ x = 75 − 56

⇒ x = 19

**∴ The correct answer is 19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Definition

The mean is the **sum** of all data points divided by the count of data points: Mean = (Σxᵢ) ÷ n.

Properties of Deviations

The algebraic **sum of deviations** of a set of observations from their **Arithmetic Mean** is always zero.

Average of AP

If numbers are in an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the **Average** is equal to the middle term (for odd n) or the mean of the two middle terms (for even n).

(i) It can monitor network usage and identify which app is using the most bandwidth.

questions.solution:

questions.question: Which irrigation technique is considered most efficient for conserving water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drip irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drip irrigation**, frequently referred to as **trickle irrigation**, is scientifically recognized as the most efficient water-application system, typically achieving efficiency levels of **90% or higher**.
 
• The process involves applying water at very low rates (typically **2 to 20 liters per hour**) through a specialized network of **plastic pipes, valves, and emitters** directly to the soil surface or the **root zone** of plants.
 
• By targeting the root zone specifically, it drastically minimizes **evapotranspiration** and **deep percolation** losses, which are prevalent in traditional irrigation methods.
 
• This technique maintains a near-optimal **soil moisture level**, preventing plants from experiencing water stress and thereby significantly improving **crop yield** and quality.
 
• It also facilitates **fertigation**, where soluble fertilizers are mixed with the water, ensuring precise **nutrient delivery** and reducing the risk of groundwater contamination from chemical leaching.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flood Irrigation**:

 
 
• A traditional **surface irrigation** method where water is pumped or brought to a field and allowed to flow over the ground freely.
 
• It is highly **inefficient** (often less than **50%**), as a large volume of water is lost to **surface runoff** and uncontrolled infiltration.
 
 
 
• **Sprinkler Irrigation**:
 
 
• Simulates **natural rainfall** by distributing water through a system of pumps and pipes, spraying it through **nozzles** into the air.
 
• While more efficient than flood methods, it remains vulnerable to **wind drift** and high **evaporation rates**, especially in arid climates.
 
 
 
• **Canal Irrigation**:
 
 
• A large-scale system utilizing man-made channels to divert water from **rivers or reservoirs** to agricultural land.
 
• It often suffers from high **conveyance losses** due to seepage and can lead to environmental issues like **waterlogging** and **soil salinity**.

questions.question: Which of the following islands/island groups of India is of coral origin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lakshadweep Islands**, located in the **Arabian Sea** off the **Malabar Coast** of **Kerala**, are entirely composed of **coral deposits**.
 
• These islands are classified as **atolls**, which are ring-shaped or horse-shoe-shaped coral reefs that partially or completely encircle a central **lagoon**.
 
• Geologically, they are situated on the **Chagos-Laccadive Ridge**, a submarine mountain range; the islands were formed by the continuous accumulation of **skeletal remains** of **coral polyps** over thousands of years.
 
• The archipelago consists of approximately **36 islands**, though only 10 are inhabited, with **Kavaratti** serving as the administrative headquarters.
 
• The total land area of this **Union Territory** is small, covering only about **32 square kilometers**, making it India's smallest Union Territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**:

 
 
• Located in the **Bay of Bengal**, these are considered the elevated portions of submerged mountain ranges, specifically an extension of the **Arakan Yoma** range in **Myanmar**.
 
• While they have **fringing coral reefs** around them, the islands themselves are **tectonic** and **volcanic** in origin.
 
• This group contains **Barren Island**, which is the only **active volcano** in South Asia.
 
 
 
• **Diu Island**:
 
 
• A small coastal island located off the southern coast of the **Kathiawar Peninsula** in **Gujarat**.
 
• It is of **sedimentary** and **tectonic origin**, separated from the mainland by a narrow creek, and is known for its **Miliolite limestone** formations.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Channels**:
 
 
• The **Ten Degree Channel** separates the **Andaman** islands from the **Nicobar** islands.
 
• The **Nine Degree Channel** separates the island of **Minicoy** from the rest of the **Lakshadweep** archipelago.
 
• The **Eight Degree Channel** separates the entire Lakshadweep group from the **Maldives**.

questions.question: Tank irrigation is mainly practiced in which of the following states of India due to uneven terrain and less rainfall?

__
 
• **Tank irrigation** is a traditional method of **water harvesting** where rainwater is collected in natural or man-made depressions, widely prevalent in the **Peninsular Plateau** of India.
 
• **Karnataka**, situated on the **Deccan Plateau**, possesses **hard crystalline rocks** and a non-porous rocky structure that makes the excavation of **canals** and **wells** extremely difficult and costly.
 
• The **undulating topography** and **uneven terrain** of the state provide natural depressions that are ideal for constructing embankments to store **monsoon runoff**.
 
• Since **rainfall** in the interior parts of the state is **seasonal** and often **insufficient**, these tanks act as essential reservoirs to sustain agriculture during the dry **rabi** and **kharif** seasons.
 
• Historical data indicates that the **Southern states**, including **Karnataka**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Tamil Nadu**, account for the highest percentage of tank-irrigated area in India due to these specific **physiographic** conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himachal Pradesh**

 
 
• Characterized by **mountainous terrain** where traditional irrigation is done through **Kuhls**, which are surface channels diverting water from **glaciers** and streams.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal**
 
 
• The state features **flat alluvial plains** and **perennial rivers**, leading to a dominance of **canal irrigation** and **tube well** systems rather than tanks.
 
 
 
• **Haryana**
 
 
• Part of the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**, this state relies heavily on **tube wells** and an extensive **canal network**, such as the **Western Yamuna Canal**, facilitated by **soft soil** and level land.

questions.question: In which of the following cases is the work done negative?

Force and displacement are in the same direction

__
 
• **Work done** is mathematically defined as the dot product of the **force vector** and the **displacement vector**. It is a **scalar quantity**.
 
• The formula for work is W = F · s · cos theta , where **F** represents the magnitude of the force, **s** represents the displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.

• **Positive Work:**

 
 
• Occurs when the angle **θ** is **acute** (between 0° and 90°).
 
• The force or a component of the force acts in the **same direction** as the displacement.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, Citizenship by incorporation of territory applies when _________________.

options.text: A citizen moves from one state to another
A foreigner resides for five years
A state is divided into two

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India acquires new territory**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Incorporation of Territory** is one of the five distinct ways to acquire Indian citizenship, as defined under **Section 7** of the **Citizenship Act, 1955**.
 
• It applies specifically when a foreign territory becomes a part of the **Indian Union** through treaty, purchase, conquest, or any other means of acquisition.
 
• The **Government of India** exercises the power to specify, via a notification in the **Official Gazette**, which persons from the newly acquired territory shall become citizens of India.
 
• Unlike birth or descent, this form of acquisition is **collective** and depends on the specific date and criteria determined by the **Central Government**.
 
• A notable historical application was the **Citizenship (Pondicherry) Order, 1962**, which granted Indian citizenship to inhabitants of **Pondicherry** (now Puducherry) after it was integrated into India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Framework**:

 
 
• **Articles 5 to 11** in **Part II** of the **Constitution of India** address citizenship, primarily defining who was a citizen at the time of the Constitution’s commencement on **January 26, 1950**.
 
• **Article 11** empowers the **Parliament** to regulate the right of citizenship by law, which led to the enactment of the comprehensive **Citizenship Act, 1955**.
 
 
 
• **Other Modes of Acquisition**:
 
 
• **Birth (Section 3)**: Citizenship based on the location and date of birth within Indian borders.
 
• **Descent (Section 4)**: Citizenship acquired by those born outside India to Indian parents.
 
• **Registration (Section 5)**: Available to **Persons of Indian Origin (PIO)** or spouses of Indian citizens after a prescribed period of residence.
 
• **Naturalization (Section 6)**: A process for foreigners who have resided in India for **12 years** and meet specific qualifications.
 
 
 
• **Single Citizenship**: India follows the principle of **Single Citizenship**, meaning there is no separate state citizenship; moving between states does not change one’s status as an Indian citizen.

questions.question: What event caused Mahatma Gandhi to withdraw the non-cooperation movement in February 1922?

options.text: A decision by the British to suspend restrictions on civil liberties.
The violent attack on policemen during the Chauri Chaura incident.

__
 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement**, which began in **1920**, was abruptly called off by **Mahatma Gandhi** in **February 1922** due to the outbreak of violence.
 
• The specific catalyst was the **Chauri Chaura** incident, which occurred on **February 4, 1922**, in the **Gorakhpur** district of the **United Provinces** (present-day Uttar Pradesh).
 
• During a protest march, a clash broke out between the volunteers and the police; the police opened fire on the crowd, which provoked the protesters to attack the local police station.
 
• The mob set the police station on fire, resulting in the death of **22 policemen** who were burned alive inside the building.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, a staunch practitioner of **Ahimsa** (non-violence), felt that the movement was deviating from its peaceful path and becoming a violent struggle.
 
• He believed that the Indian people were not yet fully prepared for a disciplined, non-violent mass movement and required further training in the principles of **Satyagraha**.
 
• On **February 12, 1922**, the **Congress Working Committee** met at **Bardoli**, where Gandhi passed a resolution to suspend the movement nationwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It involved the **boycott** of British goods, government-run educational institutions, and law courts.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Withdrawal**:
 
 
• The sudden suspension of the movement led to significant internal debate within the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• This internal rift eventually led to the formation of the **Swaraj Party** in **1923** by **Chittaranjan Das** and **Motilal Nehru**, who advocated for participating in legislative councils.

questions.question: Which of the following situations in football leads to a 'Penalty Kick' being awarded?

options.text: A player scores three consecutive goals
A foul is committed inside the penalty area
The goalkeeper handles the ball outside the goal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A foul is committed inside the penalty area**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Law 14** of the **International Football Association Board (IFAB)** Laws of the Game, a **penalty kick** is awarded if a player commits a **direct free kick** offense inside their own **penalty area**.
 
• The offense must be committed while the **ball is in play**. If the ball is out of play when the foul occurs, the restart is determined by the previous situation (e.g., goal kick, corner).
 
• Specific fouls that lead to a penalty include **tripping**, **striking**, **pushing**, **charging**, or **deliberate handball** (excluding the goalkeeper within their own area) by a defending player.
 
• The ball is placed on the **penalty mark**, which is located **11 meters (12 yards)** from the center of the **goal line**.
 
• During the kick, all players except the **kicker** and the **defending goalkeeper** must be at least **9.15 meters (10 yards)** from the penalty mark and outside the **penalty area** until the ball is kicked.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Offside:**

 
 
• Being in an **offside position** is not an offense in itself; however, if a player becomes active in play from that position, the referee awards an **indirect free kick** to the opposing team.
 
 
 
• **Goalkeeper handling outside the area:**
 
 
• The **goalkeeper** is only permitted to handle the ball within their own **penalty box**. If they touch the ball with their hands outside this area, a **direct free kick** is awarded.
 
 
 
• **Hat-trick:**
 
 
• This term refers to a single player scoring **three goals** in a single match. It is a statistical milestone and does not trigger any specific **refereeing award** like a penalty.
 
 
 
• **VAR (Video Assistant Referee):**
 
 
• In professional leagues, **VAR** can intervene to review **penalty kick** decisions, ensuring that fouls occurring on the line or inside the **18-yard box** are correctly identified.

questions.question: What does RAM stand for in a computer system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Random Access Memory**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Random Access Memory (RAM)** is the primary **internal memory** of a computer system that allows data items to be read or written in almost the same amount of time irrespective of the physical location of data inside the memory.
 
• It serves as a **temporary storage** area or **working space** for the **Operating System**, application programs, and data currently in use, enabling the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** to access instructions quickly.
 
• RAM is fundamentally **volatile** in nature, which means that any information stored within it is lost immediately when the **power supply** is interrupted or the computer is turned off.
 
• The performance of a system is heavily dependent on the **capacity** and **speed** of the RAM, as higher RAM allows for more efficient **multitasking** and faster execution of complex software.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dynamic RAM (DRAM)**

 
 
• This is the most common type of RAM used in modern computers; it utilizes **capacitors** to store bits of data and requires **frequent refreshing** to prevent data loss.
 
 
 
• **Static RAM (SRAM)**
 
 
• Unlike DRAM, SRAM does not need to be refreshed and is significantly **faster**; however, it is more expensive and bulkier, typically used for high-speed **CPU Cache** memory.
 
 
 
• **Read-Only Memory (ROM)**
 
 
• In contrast to RAM, **ROM** is **non-volatile** memory, meaning it retains its data even without power; it is used to store the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)** or firmware that initializes hardware during the **boot-up process**.
 
 
 
• **SDRAM (Synchronous DRAM)**
 
 
• A specialized version of DRAM that **synchronizes** its speed with the **system clock**, increasing the number of instructions the processor can execute in a given time.

questions.question: Which season in India is characterised by hot, dry winds known as ‘Loo’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Summer season**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Summer season** in India, which lasts from **March to May**, is characterized by a rapid rise in temperature and a decrease in air pressure over the northern parts of the country.
 
• The **Loo** is a striking feature of this season, consisting of strong, gusty, hot, and dry winds that blow during the day over **North and Northwestern India**.
 
• These winds are primarily caused by the intense heating of the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**, creating a localized low-pressure system that attracts dry air from the **Thar Desert**.
 
• Temperatures during a **Loo** event typically range between **45°C and 50°C**, often persisting into the evening and causing severe discomfort.
 
• Direct exposure to these hot winds is extremely dangerous and can lead to fatal conditions such as **heatstroke**, **hyperthermia**, and **severe dehydration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pre-monsoon showers**:

 
 
• Occur towards the end of the summer season, providing relief from the intense heat through localized thunderstorms.
 
• In **Kerala** and **Karnataka**, they are known as **Mango Showers** as they aid in the early ripening of mangoes; in **West Bengal**, they are called **Kaal Baisakhi**.
 
 
 
• **Cold weather season**:
 
 
• Spans from **mid-November to February** in Northern India, characterized by clear skies, low temperatures, and low humidity.

questions.question: As of November 2025, Article 1 of the Indian Constitution classifies Indian territory into how many distinct categories under Constitutional provisions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 1** of the **Constitution of India** defines the name and territory of the Union, establishing that **India**, that is **Bharat**, shall be a **Union of States**.
 
• Under **Article 1(3)**, the **territory of India** is classified into **three** distinct categories: the **territories of the States**, the **Union Territories**, and **territories that may be acquired** by the Government of India at any time.
 
• The first category includes **28 States** (as of 2025) which are members of the **federal system** and share a distribution of powers with the Central Government.
 
• The second category comprises the **Union Territories** specified in the **First Schedule** (currently **8 UTs**), which are governed directly by the **President** through an administrator appointed by him.
 
• The third category refers to **acquired territories**, which allows India to incorporate new lands through international legal methods such as **cession**, **occupation**, or **conquest**, even though no such territory is currently held separately from the existing states/UTs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Territory of India vs. Union of India**:

 
 
• The expression **Territory of India** is wider than the **Union of India** because the **Union** includes only the **States**, whereas the **Territory** encompasses States, Union Territories, and any acquired areas.
 
• While States are **federal units**, Union Territories and acquired territories are **unitary units** administered directly by the **Union Government**.
 
 
 
• **First Schedule**:
 
 
• The **First Schedule** contains the names of the **States** and **Union Territories** along with their **territorial extent** and boundaries.
 
• Any modification to the **First Schedule** or the **Fourth Schedule** resulting from the creation or reorganization of states under **Article 2** or **Article 3** is not considered a formal amendment under **Article 368**.
 
 
 
• **Sovereignty and Acquisition**:
 
 
• Being a **sovereign state**, India has the inherent right to acquire **foreign territories**. Historical examples of such acquisitions include **Dadra and Nagar Haveli**, **Goa**, **Daman and Diu**, **Puducherry**, and **Sikkim**, which were later integrated into the standard state/UT categories.

questions.question: What was a significant objective of the fiscal and monetary policy reforms initiated in India post 1991?

__
 
• Following the **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis** in **1991**, India initiated structural reforms to shift from a centrally planned economy to a **market-led economy**.
 
• A primary objective of the **monetary policy reforms** was the **deregulation of interest rates**, allowing banks to determine rates based on market demand and supply rather than rigid **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** directives.
 
• The **Narasimham Committee (1991)** on the Financial System recommended reducing the **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** and **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** to increase the availability of lendable funds for the private sector, thereby **enhancing financial sector efficiency**.
 
• **Fiscal policy reforms** focused on **macroeconomic stabilization** by reducing the **fiscal deficit**, which had reached 8.4% of the GDP in **1990-91**, through better expenditure management and tax restructuring.
 
• These reforms aimed to create a **competitive banking environment** by allowing the entry of new **private sector banks** and increasing the operational autonomy of public sector banks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **New Economic Policy (NEP) 1991**:

 
 
• **Liberalization**: Involved removing **industrial licensing**, dismantling price controls, and allowing **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** to integrate with the global economy.
 
• **Fiscal Reforms**: Based on the **Raja Chelliah Committee** recommendations, these reforms simplified the tax structure and lowered **corporate tax** and **personal income tax** rates to improve compliance.
 
• **Monetary Shift**: The **RBI** transitioned from direct controls to indirect instruments like the **Repo Rate** and **Open Market Operations (OMO)** to manage liquidity.
 
• **External Sector**: The **Indian Rupee** was devalued in **July 1991** and later moved toward a **unified exchange rate system** to boost exports and attract foreign capital.

• **Hardware**:

questions.question: In which year was the Indian freedom fighter **Tantia Tope**, a prominent leader of the Revolt of 1857, executed by the British?

• **Tantia Tope**, born as **Ramachandra Pandurang Tope** in **1814**, was one of the most distinguished military leaders of the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• He was a close associate of **Nana Sahib** and served as the commander-in-chief of the rebel forces in **Cawnpore (Kanpur)**.
 
• Following the fall of **Kanpur**, he joined forces with **Rani Lakshmi Bai** to defend **Jhansi** and later helped in the capture of **Gwalior**.
 
• After the death of **Rani Lakshmi Bai** in June **1858**, Tantia Tope successfully conducted a brilliant **guerrilla warfare** campaign against the British for nearly a year across **Central India** and **Rajasthan**.
 
• He was ultimately betrayed by his trusted friend **Man Singh**, the Raja of Narwar, while resting in the **Paron** forests.
 
• He was captured by British forces on **April 7, 1859**, and subsequently tried by a military court at **Shivpuri**.
 
• Tantia Tope was executed by hanging on **April 18, 1859**, at **Shivpuri**, Madhya Pradesh, which effectively signaled the end of the major armed resistance of **1857**.

questions.question: What will be the resultant force if a body of mass 10 kg is moving with an acceleration of 5m/sec²?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50 Newton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **force**, **mass**, and **acceleration** is governed by **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, which states that the force acting on an object is directly proportional to the product of its mass and acceleration.
 
• The mathematical formula for this law is **F = m × a**, where **F** represents the **resultant force**, **m** is the **mass** of the object, and **a** is the **acceleration**.
 
• In the given problem, the **mass (m)** of the body is **10 kg** and the **acceleration (a)** is **5 m/s²**.
 
• By applying the formula: **Force (F) = 10 kg × 5 m/s² = 50 kg·m/s²**.
 
• The unit **kg·m/s²** is equivalent to the **Newton (N)**, which is the standard **SI unit** of force. Therefore, the resultant force is **50 Newton**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton (N)**:

 
 
• It is the **derived unit** of **force** in the **International System of Units (SI)**.
 
• One Newton is defined as the force needed to provide a mass of **one kilogram** with an acceleration of **one meter per second squared**.
 
 
 
• **Joule (J)**:
 
 
• The **Joule** is the **SI unit** of **work**, **energy**, and **heat**.
 
• It is not a unit of force; hence, option 4 (**2 Joule**) is conceptually incorrect for a force calculation.
 
• One Joule is equal to the work done by a force of **one Newton** acting through a distance of **one meter**.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion**:
 
 
• **First Law**: An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force (**Inertia**).
 
• **Third Law**: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.question: Which of the following SI prefixes has a multiplicative factor of 10–⁹ ?

• Derived from the Greek word **nanos** (meaning dwarf), it is symbolized by the lowercase letter **'n'** and is frequently used in **nanotechnology**, **microelectronics**, and **molecular physics** to measure distances at the atomic scale, such as **nanometers (nm)**.
 
• The use of these prefixes was formally established and expanded by the **General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM)** to ensure global uniformity in scientific and commercial measurements.

• **Milli**: Denoted by the symbol **'m'**, it signifies a factor of **10−³** (one-thousandth). Common applications include **millimeters (mm)** and **milligrams (mg)**.
 
• **Centi**: Represented by the symbol **'c'**, it indicates a factor of **10−²** (one-hundredth). It is most familiarly used in **centimeters (cm)** for everyday length measurements.

questions.question: The main aim of globalisation in India was to____.

options.text: Increase and maintain higher trade barriers

• The primary objective was the **economic integration** of the domestic market with the **global economy**, effectively ending the era of an inward-looking, closed economic system.
 
• This process involved the systematic reduction of **trade barriers**, including the slashing of high **customs duties** and the removal of **quantitative restrictions** (quotas) on imports and exports.
 
• By facilitating the free flow of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, technology, and services, India aimed to enhance the **competitiveness** of its domestic industries on an international scale.

• Involves the **disinvestment** of government equity in **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** to improve efficiency, accountability, and fiscal discipline within the economy.
 
 
 
• **Self-Sufficiency and Protectionism**

questions.question: In which year did Junagadh district gain recognition for organizing the country’s first-ever Lok Adalat at Una?

__
 
• The first **Lok Adalat** camp in post-independence India was organized in the state of **Gujarat** on **March 14, 1982**.
 
• This historic event took place at **Una** in the **Junagadh** district, marking the formal beginning of the modern people's court system in the country.
 
• The initiative was spearheaded by **Justice P.N. Bhagwati**, who was then a judge of the **Supreme Court of India** and a major proponent of legal aid for the poor.
 
• The primary goal of organizing this **Lok Adalat** was to settle disputes through **conciliation**, **mediation**, and **compromise**, providing a faster alternative to the traditional, time-consuming judicial process.
 
• The success of the **Una** experiment led to the nationwide adoption of the **Lok Adalat** mechanism as a key component of the **Alternative Dispute Resolution** (ADR) system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Adalat System**:

 
 
• It is based on **Gandhian principles** and is often referred to as the **People's Court**.
 
• The system is designed to provide **free legal aid** and ensure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity, as mandated by **Article 39A** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The awards passed by a **Lok Adalat** are deemed to be a decree of a **civil court** and are final and binding on all parties; no appeal lies against such awards in any court of law.
 
 
 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**:
 
 
• Although the first camp was held in **1982**, the **Lok Adalat** system was given statutory status only after the enactment of this Act, which came into force on **November 9, 1995**.
 
• The Act led to the establishment of the **National Legal Services Authority** (NALSA) to oversee legal aid programs across the nation.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction**:
 
 
• **Lok Adalats** have the power to deal with cases pending before any court (at any stage) and also matters at the **pre-litigation** stage.
 
• They typically handle **matrimonial disputes**, **land acquisition cases**, **labor disputes**, and **compoundable criminal offenses**.

questions.question: Suspension of enforcement of Fundamental Rights except Articles 20 and 21 occurs under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 359**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 359** of the **Indian Constitution** empowers the **President** to suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** during the operation of a **National Emergency**.
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** introduced a significant safeguard by stipulating that the **President** cannot suspend the right to move the court for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed by **Article 20** and **Article 21**.
 
• **Article 20** provides protection in respect of **conviction for offences**, while **Article 21** guarantees the **protection of life and personal liberty**; these are considered the most basic rights that remain enforceable even during an emergency.
 
• Unlike **Article 358**, which automatically suspends the freedoms under **Article 19** (such as speech and assembly) upon a proclamation of emergency due to war or external aggression, **Article 359** does not automatically suspend any rights.
 
• Suspension under **Article 359** only occurs when the **President** issues a specific **Presidential Order** naming the particular **Fundamental Rights** whose enforcement is to be suspended.
 
• The **Presidential Order** must be submitted to each **House of Parliament** as soon as possible for approval after it is issued.

• Deals with the proclamation of a **National Emergency** by the **President**.
 
• Such a proclamation can be made on the grounds of **war**, **external aggression**, or **armed rebellion**.
 
 
 
• **Article 353**:
 
 
• Describes the **effects** of the proclamation of emergency on the distribution of powers.
 
• It grants the **Union** the authority to extend its **executive power** to give directions to any **State**.
 
 
 
• **Article 360**:
 
 
• Contains provisions regarding **Financial Emergency**.
 
• It can be declared if the **President** is satisfied that the **financial stability** or credit of **India** or any part of its territory is threatened.

questions.question: Which of the following file formats does not get affected by the destination format and version?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**.pdf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Portable Document Format (.pdf)** was developed by **Adobe** in **1993** to present documents, including text formatting and images, in a manner independent of application software, hardware, and **operating systems**.
 
• The **PDF format** is a **fixed-layout** file type, meaning it preserves the exact **visual appearance** of the document; it embeds **fonts**, **images**, and **vector graphics** so they do not shift or change when opened on a different **destination device**.
 
• Because the file is essentially a **digital snapshot** of the final document, it is not affected by the **software version** used to view it, ensuring that **pagination** and **alignment** remain identical to the original creation.
 
• Unlike editable document formats, **PDFs** do not rely on the fonts installed on the **recipient system**, which prevents the common issue of **font substitution** that ruins document aesthetics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Editable Microsoft Formats**:

 
 
• **.ppt and .pptx**: These are **Microsoft PowerPoint** formats. **.ppt** is the older **binary format**, while **.pptx** is the **XML-based** standard. Both are highly susceptible to **formatting errors**, missing **animations**, or **media playback** issues if the **destination version** of Office differs from the source.
 
• **.docx**: This is the default **Microsoft Word** format. It is **reflowable**, meaning the **layout** can change based on **printer settings**, **screen resolution**, or the specific **word processor version** (e.g., Word 2010 vs. Word 365), often causing **text wrapping** or **image displacement**.
 
• **Standardization**: In **2008**, PDF was released as an **open standard (ISO 32000-1)**, further cementing its role as the global standard for **secure** and **consistent** document sharing.

questions.question: Name the popular technique used by the Harappans for casting bronze.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lost-Wax Technique**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Harappan Civilization** (Indus Valley Civilization) was highly proficient in metallurgy, particularly in the production of bronze icons using the **Lost-Wax Technique**, also known as **Cire Perdue**.
 
• In this process, a model was first made of **wax** and then coated with a thick layer of **clay**; once the clay dried, the structure was heated so the wax melted and was drained out through a tiny hole.
 
• Molten **bronze**, which is an alloy typically composed of **copper** and **tin**, was then poured into the hollow clay mold to take the shape of the original wax model.
 
• The most famous example of this technique from the ancient world is the **Dancing Girl** statue discovered at **Mohenjo-daro**, dating back to approximately **2500 BCE**.
 
• Archaeological evidence shows that bronze casting was practiced on a wide scale, with significant findings including a **copper dog** and **bird** from **Lothal** and a **bronze buffalo** from **Kalibangan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sand Casting Technique**:

 
 
• Utilizes a mold made of **silica sand** and a bonding agent. While common in modern industrial casting for engine blocks and heavy machinery, it lacks the fine detail capability used for ancient Harappan artistic figurines.
 
 
 
• **Die Casting Technique**:
 
 
• A modern manufacturing process where molten metal is forced under high pressure into reusable metal molds called **dies**. This method was developed in the **19th century** for mass production.
 
 
 
• **Open Mould Casting**:
 
 
• The simplest form of casting where metal is poured into an open cavity carved into stone or clay. It was primarily used by early civilizations for flat tools like **flat axes**, **chisels**, and **knives** rather than complex three-dimensional sculptures.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of structural unemployment?

options.text: A worker loses their job due to seasonal fluctuations in tourism
A textile worker loses the job due to industry automation
A worker is laid off during a temporary dip in demand
A person quits a job to pursue higher education

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A textile worker loses the job due to industry automation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Structural unemployment** is a long-term form of unemployment caused by fundamental shifts in an economy, leading to a **mismatch** between the skills workers possess and the skills demanded by employers.
 
• It often occurs due to **technological advancements**, such as **automation** or **robotics**, which render specific manual or cognitive tasks obsolete within an industry.
 
• In the case of a **textile worker** losing their job to **industry automation**, the worker is displaced because machines can now perform their role more efficiently, making their specific skillset redundant in the current economic structure.
 
• Unlike other types of unemployment, structural issues cannot be solved simply by an economic upturn; they require workers to undergo significant **retraining** or **vocational education** to acquire new, relevant competencies.
 
• Other contributing factors to structural unemployment include **globalization**, which may lead to the outsourcing of manufacturing jobs, and changes in **consumer preferences** that cause entire industries to decline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional Unemployment**:

 
 
• This is a **temporary** state where workers are in the process of moving from one job to another or are entering the labor market for the first time.
 
• It is often considered **voluntary** and is a sign of a flexible labor market where individuals seek better-matching roles.
 
 
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment**:
 
 
• This type is directly tied to the **business cycle**, specifically during **economic recessions** or downturns.
 
• When the **aggregate demand** for goods and services falls, businesses reduce production and lay off workers, as seen in a **temporary dip in demand**.
 
 
 
• **Seasonal Unemployment**:
 
 
• This occurs when the demand for labor changes according to the **time of year** or specific **seasons**.
 
• It is prevalent in sectors like **tourism**, **agriculture**, and **construction**, where activities are restricted by weather or holiday cycles.

questions.question: Which pancreatic hormone regulates blood glucose levels by stimulating the uptake of glucose by body cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insulin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulin** is a critical **peptide hormone** secreted by the **beta cells** of the **Islets of Langerhans** within the **pancreas**.
 
• It serves as the primary **anabolic hormone** in humans, responsible for regulating **metabolism** by promoting the absorption of glucose from the blood into **liver**, **fat**, and **skeletal muscle** cells.
 
• The hormone functions by binding to **insulin receptors** on target cells, which triggers the translocation of **GLUT4** (glucose transporter type 4) to the cell membrane, facilitating **glucose uptake**.
 
• In the liver and muscle tissues, **insulin** stimulates **glycogenesis**, the biochemical process of converting glucose into **glycogen** for long-term storage.
 
• It plays a vital role in maintaining **blood glucose homeostasis**; a deficiency or mismanagement of this hormone leads to **Diabetes Mellitus**, characterized by chronically high blood sugar levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glucagon**:

 
 
• Secreted by the **alpha cells** of the **pancreas**.
 
• Acts as an antagonist to insulin by increasing blood glucose levels through **glycogenolysis** (breakdown of glycogen) and **gluconeogenesis**.
 
 
 
• **Cortisol**:
 
 
• A **steroid hormone** or **glucocorticoid** produced by the **adrenal cortex**.
 
• It increases blood sugar through **gluconeogenesis**, especially during periods of **stress** or fasting.
 
 
 
• **Thyroxine (T4)**:
 
 
• A major hormone secreted by the **thyroid gland** that contains **iodine**.
 
• It primarily regulates the body's **Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)** and influences the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids.
